transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora, and I've just completed your post-cataract surgery follow-up check. 

Do you have any questions about your surgery or your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora! Yes, I do have a few questions. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Great question! You can start doing light gardening after 1 week following your surgery. However, you should avoid any strenuous or heavy exercise for a full month after your operation.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you, that's helpful to know. My next question is: when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a good question. If you were using eye gel for dry eyes before your surgery, it's safe to continue using it now, unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor.

If you're not sure about the specific instructions for your eye gel, I'd recommend checking with your GP or the pharmacy.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks for clearing that up. The next thing I wanted to ask is, I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended:
It's quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, we'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to assess it further. In that case, please get in touch with your care team.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Okay, thank you for explaining that. My last question is, should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's quite common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after surgery, and it should improve quickly and settle down over time.

How long ago was your surgery? That will help me give you better guidance on what to expect.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: My surgery was about a week ago.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's helpful to know. Since it's been about a week, some blurriness is still quite normal at this stage. It should continue to improve and clear up as time goes on.

However, if your vision is getting significantly worse or stays blurry, we may need to check it to make sure everything is okay.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, I think that's all for now. Thank you for your help, Dora!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're welcome! Just to confirm, have all your questions been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, they've all been answered. Thanks again!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Wonderful! I'm glad I could help. Take care, and best of luck with your recovery!
